manifest.hypothesis: GET /api/user/:name/icon is 46% of all requests and every one reads the icon blob from MySQL (SELECT image FROM icons: 9182 calls, 51s before indexes) and hashes it; the benchmarker sends If-None-Match with the sha256 it already holds on most of those calls (seen with tcpdump on :8080 during a run), and every user response recomputes icon_hash from the blob. Keeping the hash per user in memory (filled on upload, on first read, cleared on /initialize) lets the icon endpoint answer 304 without touching the blob and lets fillUserResponse skip the blob read.

observations.summary: request table: GET /api/user/:id/icon 1650 of 3616 requests (46%); digests: SELECT image FROM icons WHERE user_id=? 9182 calls 50.9s (pre-index); tcpdump sample during load: 417 icon GETs, ~400 carrying If-None-Match with a quoted sha256

allowedChanges.reason: in-memory user id -> icon hash map, ETag matching
getIconHandler answers 304 on If-None-Match and sets ETag; postIconHandler updates the cache; fillUserResponse reads the hash from the cache

manifest.changeSummary: icon hash cached in memory per user; 304 Not Modified when If-None-Match names it; icon_hash in user responses from the cache instead of hashing the blob
manifest.expectedEffect: most icon GETs become 304 with one users lookup and no blob transfer; icons blob reads drop from ~9k to the number of uploads plus misses; score up well over 3% from the freed MySQL/app time (baseline median 6725)

ruleDecision.reason: median improved 1953 bp >= 300 bp and worst candidate 7907 > best baseline 6815

reason: icon hash cached in memory, 304 on If-None-Match: median 6725 -> 7931 (+18%); the 5077 baseline sample was taken under the slow log before the observed flag existed
